items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mack Walker and I were room mates and always have been when travelling.

ctx.x: Mack Walker and I were room mates and always have been when travelling. In Springfield Frankie Newton and I were room mates. Mack and I started getting acquainted with Harlem from 125th Street up to the Savoy, Lenox Avenue over to 8th Avenue which had an elevated line, the first I had ever seen. The streets were dirty but the city itself and the pleasure I was having taking in the sights was very exciting.

I had been told about a cabaret called Small's Paradise, so Cecil took Mack and I there during the week that we were waiting to play the New Years holidays at the Savoy. He had told me as I said before about the place but nothing about the band that was playing there. The leader was a pianist named Charlie Johnson and we had gone to Smalls quite early as Cecil said the first show was always the best to see.

The band started and Charlie Johnson left the piano and I never saw him anymore that night. But what a band! it had been quite some time back when I heard Fletcher Henderson and here I was listening to an orchestra that was in the same class as Fletcher and I had never heard of the band before. There was an outstanding trumpet player who played fast, clean as a whistle and also used a derby which he waved over the bell of the horn to get an open horn wa-wa effect.
